title: Establish service-fidelity contracts and automated SLO escalation playground
creator: Priya Rao
description: Define a clear set of service-fidelity contracts (SLOs + acceptable quality degradation bands) for hosted inference endpoints, and build an automated 'escalation playground' in staging that can simulate error-budget burn, validate rollback kinetics, and exercise automated escalation policies. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and deliverables for the PM and reliability engineering partners.
slo_targets: Interactive chat (tier-1): p50 < 70ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for first-token latency (streaming first-token metric)
Batch generation (background): median throughput targets per GPU to be captured in runtime-1.21 perf profile
Uptime SLA for hosted API: 99.9% monthly for tier-1 customers, 99.5% for free-tier
error_budget_policy: Error budget defined as 1 - availability SLA over rolling 30-day window
Tier-1 monthly error budget: 43.2 minutes of downtime (for 99.9% SLA)
Automated throttles kick in when rolling burn rate > 2x baseline for 10 minutes
If burn rate > 4x baseline for 30 minutes then escalate to human-on-call and route new traffic to fallback model variant
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (preflight): smoke tests in staging with synthetic load and correctness checks pass
Gate 1 (canary): <=5% traffic to new config, p95 latency increase <= +10% and error budget burn rate <= 1.5x over 1 hour
Gate 2 (ramp): step increments of 5-15% with 30-minute observation windows and automatic rollback on rapid burn (>3x) or p99 latency regressions > +20%
Gate 3 (full): 100% only after 72 hours of stable metrics and no sustained error budget burn
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative PRD that defines SLOs per workload class (interactive, embeddings, batch) and acceptable fidelity degradation bands for cost/latency trade-offs
Console UI exposes these SLOs and shows rolling error budget, burn rate, and remaining budget per tenant
Automated 'escalation playground' in staging that can simulate sustained latency increases, partial region failures, and model fallback, and produces reproducible test results
Runbook for on-call that prescribes actions for burn-rate tiers and includes automated rollback triggers
CI job that validates rollout gate checks for any runtime or routing policy change with mocked load
acceptance_test_plan: Create synthetic workloads that mimic 3 tenant classes and drive error budget consumption predictably
Simulate KV cache degradation to measure latency shift and verify automatic fallback to model-variant path
Introduce region-level network degradation in staging and confirm routing policy falls back within configured SLO thresholds
Run end-to-end canary where the automated gate performs rollback within 5 minutes of threshold breach and emits incident ticket
notes: Prefer per-tenant visibility for error budgets to reduce blast radius and enable tenant-specific throttles
Trade-off: stricter p99 targets increase cost; include quantization and batching recommendations as mitigations in the PRD
Decision: initial rollout will target hosted API only; Dedicated and Private will adopt policy templates later
We must align wording of 'availability' with legal SLA definitions used by Sales and Contracts
